$comment: Ground truth for gate-in extraction. Three photos are taken at the barrier
— the bill, the vehicle, and the vendor's weigh slip — and each has its own
endpoint and its own entry below.
The design principle throughout: the model reads, the server decides. Gemini
is asked only for what is printed or written. Every derived number is
arithmetic done server-side, where it is testable.
Both documents carry their own internal check, which is what makes that
possible:
bill  — quantityKg / 100 * ratePerQuintal == amount
slip  — gross - tare == net
And they check each other: the handwritten weight on the bill IS the net on
the weigh slip. See crossChecks at the bottom.

bills.source: Shayan Enterprise, Tilapatty, Kharupetia, Dist. Darrang (Assam)
bills.note: The reference bill named in docs/procurement-plan.md.
traps: The Qnty column reads '401 Pm' — a bag count, not the weight.
The billed weight is handwritten in the particulars cell: 'wt 24380'.
The rate's middle digit reads convincingly as 2810; only 2310 closes the arithmetic. A confident misread here overpays by Rs 1,21,900 on one truck.
'Party Name: Amino Farms' is the BUYER. The vendor is the letterhead.

bills.source: Shayan Enterprise, Tilapatty, Kharupetia, Dist. Darrang (Assam)
bills.note: Second bill from the same vendor, and the one with a full photo set — vehicle and weigh slip below are the same truck.
bills.arithmetic: 40790 kg = 407.90 qtl x Rs 2310/qtl = Rs 9,42,249 — exact to the rupee.
traps: The Qnty column reads '666 Pkt' — a bag count, not the weight.
The billed weight is handwritten below the particulars: 'wt 40790'.
Rate 2310 is per quintal; per-kg is 23.10 and must be derived server-side.
The truck number's third digit is ambiguous between 2 and 7. It is 1723, confirmed by the number plate and the weigh slip — a plate has no check digit, so only corroboration settles it.

$comment: THE IMPORTANT THING ABOUT THESE TWO: they are from different
weighbridges four kilometres apart and share no layout at all.
Shanti prints Gross / Tare / Net. Prem prints First Wt / Second Wt /
Net Wt, where first happens to be the empty weight and second the
loaded one — but that ordering is not guaranteed, it is just the order
the truck happened to cross the platform.
So the extractor must NOT hunt for the words 'gross' and 'tare'. It
reads whatever weights are printed and the server decides: the larger
is gross, the smaller is tare, and net must equal the difference. Same
read/decide split as the bill, for the same reason.
weighslips.source: Prem Weigh Bridge, Near HP Petrol Pump NH-15, Kharupetia, Darrang, Assam
weighslips.note: Public Weighing Ticket layout — labels the two weighings First/Second rather than tare/gross.
weighslips.arithmetic: 31730 - 7350 = 24380 — and 24380 is exactly the handwritten weight on bill 517.
traps: 'First Wt 7350' is the TARE and 'Second Wt 31730' is the GROSS. Reading them positionally as gross-then-tare inverts the load and yields a negative net.
Both weighings are seconds apart (11:45:48 and 11:45:51), so the tare was a stored figure rather than a second trip across the platform.

weighslips.source: Shanti Weigh Bridge, Panbari Road Ward No-7, Kharupetia, PIN-784115
weighslips.note: The vendor's own slip for bill 518. Dot-matrix print, not handwriting — a much easier read than the bill, which is why it can go to the cheaper model.
traps: Gross and tare carry their own dates and times; both are 13/08/2026 15:41 here, meaning the vehicle was weighed loaded and the tare was a stored figure rather than a second trip.
Party name and Item are blank on the form. Absence is not a read failure.

vehicles.note: Front-on photo of the same truck at the gate, taken with a stamping camera app that burns GPS and time into the image.
traps: The photo carries a large burnt-in text overlay with its own date and place. The plate must be read from the number plate itself, never from the overlay.

The overlay date (14 Aug) is the day AFTER the bill and slip (13 Aug) — the truck was loaded and weighed one day and arrived the next. Arrival date and bill date are different things and neither should be derived from the other.

$comment: What the three photos prove about each other. These are server-side checks
across documents, and they are the strongest signal available at the gate —
each one turns an unverifiable handwritten field into a corroborated one.

checks.name: plate agrees across all three
checks.on518: AS26AC1723 on all three — this is what settled the ambiguous digit
checks.onFailure: flag plate_mismatch, confirm with the guard (V9). Never block.

checks.name: the slip's net IS the bill's weight
checks.why: The handwritten weight on the bill is copied from this slip. Cross-checking them turns the single most error-prone field on the bill into a verified one, and catches a misread digit that the bill's own arithmetic would happily accept.
